Rate Card — Distance Pricing (RideGuru style)

Used by Estimate by Distance and the Fare Estimate tab. Fare = base + (per-mile × miles) + (per-minute × minutes) + booking fee, never below the minimum. Airport flats override everything.

The rate book prices every booking automatically (all-day flat). Tick zones as “20 Area” below. The airport flat (LGA/JFK) applies only when the non-airport end is in the 20 area; farther zones price from the book. A remembered per-route price beats the rate book, so special deals stick.

Built to your exact accepted submission format (file b01593_20260101-20260131.csv): the 16 columns in order — dispatching_base_number, pickup_date, pickup_time, TLC_drivers_license_number, license_plate, affiliated_base_number, pickup_location_type, pickup_location_name, pickup_longitude, pickup_latitude, dropoff_date, dropoff_time, dropoff_location_type, dropoff_location_name, dropoff_longitude, dropoff_latitude. Dates are written M/D/YYYY, times 24-hour, line endings CRLF, comma-delimited with double-quote escaping. Location type auto-classifies as Exact Address / Airport / Intersection Off (intersections written "STREET N STREET BOROUGH"); longitude/latitude are left blank (address is sufficient). Filename: baselicense_yyyymmdd-yyyymmdd.csv. TLC may revise the spec, so confirm on nyc.gov/tlc before each submission.
Reminder: as of May 28, 2026, each upload also needs the TLC Affirmation (true-and-accurate report, or no-dispatch affidavit), submitted on the TLC site. CSVs go via SFTP/portal. Drop-off data is required on every trip; keep records 18 months.

Import from your old system (FoxPro / CSV / Excel)

Bring your FoxPro data into Skyway. Export each FoxPro table to a CSV file (steps at the bottom), then load them here one at a time. Your columns can be named anything — you map them in the next step. Existing records aren't duplicated.

Caller ID history: none loaded — loads who's-calling recognition & auto-fill from your BaseI Jobs Report.
Historical route prices: none loaded — feeds real fares into the fare checker & auto-prices repeat routes.
Web bookings feed:
Driver IQ history: none loaded — seeds Driver IQ from your 91k-trip archive (regular customers, busy times, airport runs).
How to export your FoxPro tables to CSV
Easiest (no FoxPro needed): your data lives in .DBF files inside the FoxPro program's folder (for example CUST.DBF, TRIPS.DBF). Open each one in the free LibreOffice Calc (it opens .dbf directly), then File → Save As → Text CSV. Load that CSV here.
From inside FoxPro: in the Command Window, for each table type:
USE cust  then  COPY TO cust.csv TYPE CSV
Repeat for your trips, drivers and vehicle tables.
Order matters: import Accounts and Addresses first, then Drivers and Vehicles, then Trips last — so each trip can link to the customers and drivers already loaded.

How to use Skyway — the 4 basics
1
Take the call & book it. On the Dispatch screen, type who's riding, where they're going from and to, then press the green Book Trip button. Start typing an address and pick it from the list — the price fills in by itself.
2
Find it on the board. The trip drops into the Upcoming Reservations sheet below, and moves up to Active / Due Now as pickup time gets close.
3
Give it a driver & car. On the trip's row, use the Driver and Vehicle drop-downs. A green ✓ means the car fits; a red ⚠ means it's the wrong type or too small.
4
Move it along. Press Dispatch when the car heads out, Complete when the ride is done. If the ride falls through, press Cancel; if the rider never shows, press No-Show.
Tip: Open extra windows from the toolbar (Pop out) and drag them to other screens — one for taking calls, one for the board. They all stay in sync. Everything saves on this computer automatically; use Settings → Export Backup once a day to keep a copy.
